# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-17

**A new long-form is uploaded and scheduled, “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN”. It is not the Ravana long-form, which is due on 19 November with no draft on disk. The newest film Short is behind the usual on day two, a sign the film window is closing.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish the Ravana fact-check long-form: who first argued that Ravana was the wronged side.** (long, due 2026-11-19, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: The three Ravana Shorts hold 75,695, 71,062 and 30,044 views, and searches for Ravana and Sai Pallavi still land only on Shorts. Over the 365-day window a long-form view brings 8.63x the subscribers a Shorts view does. The Indonesia long-form does not answer these viewers. Two days left, no draft on disk.  
   First step: Tonight, write the first minute: open on the 1882 sentence itself, on screen, and name its author after it, checked against the book; stay with him to 0:30. Have the draft on disk by tomorrow night.
2. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: The Karnataka row over his legacy has been in the news since 11 November and nothing is scripted. The owner's note of 15 November sets the story: the prize money and palace treasure taken on 4 May 1799, then the British writing of Tipu as a tyrant. His birth date is disputed, so the Short rests on the news, not on the birthday.  
   First step: Finish the script today from the prize records and Wellesley's dispatches: one sum or one object that shows who got rich, checked against the original, as sentence one. Record tomorrow.
3. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: It is the top-ranked dated moment of the next three weeks and it sits with Aurangzeb, the subject of the channel's two largest videos. Videos that size brought 66.4% of lifetime subscribers, and this month none has come: 0 subscribers against 1,005 planned from them.  
   First step: Today, gather the named sources for the order. Then write sentence one as the order, the place and the date, told as an act of state, not a martyrdom story. Put his name at the front of the title.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
17,600 subscribers against a target of 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 18,849, which needs 51.5 net a day; the 7-day rate is 67.1 and the 28-day rate 34.3. Projection basis: 7-day rate. On that basis the month ends at 18,473, 376 short, and the channel is 532 behind the ramp today. The 7-day rate rests on the film week, so do not read it as the new normal. Correction: yesterday's brief said most growth now comes from the videos. Today uploads account for 49.1% of net subscribers over 28 days, under half, so the rate also rests on growth outside the videos that can stop without warning. The lever furthest behind is breakouts: 0 subscribers against 1,005 targeted this month. 0.72 of a breakout at the median 1,393 subs. The demonstrated route is a newsjack of a mass release (Chhava gave three of four) or an evergreen controversy with a searchable name; check the calendar and news releases for the next peg. Long-form did 69,960 views in the 7 days to 2026-11-14, level with the week before (-0.8%), but its last two days counted were its lowest of the fortnight, 3,901 on the last. Shorts did 138,481 against 57,145, most of it one Ravana Short on 11 November. Last week's two Shorts that beat the usual were both about Ravana, which is why the Ravana long-form stays first.

What's working
- The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 11.9 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the Ravana long-form's shape: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”
- A second Ramayana long-form is ready: “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN” is uploaded and scheduled. Its title states a claim, the check both earlier Ramayana long-forms failed in their post-mortems.
- “Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” keeps earning from search: 9,426 views, with steady daily views for ten days and no decay, as searches for “ram setu” and “adams bridge” land on it. A Short that answers a searched name keeps working.

What's wrong
- Long-form has run down and the last release did not stop it. “Ramayana’s Many Versions” stands at 8,324 views and 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000, 8 days after release. Probable cause, from its post-mortem: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: the Indonesia long-form. At day three, compare its first drop after the opening with the 14 points “Ramayana’s Many Versions” lost at 0:35.
- Film reach is still not turning into subscribers. “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8.5, and only 41.3% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of the fall is how views are now counted. Probable cause: the film videos answer a scene or tour a map, and none names a culprit. Test: the Ravana long-form, which names one; compare its subscribers per 1,000 on day three with the Asia long-form's.
- The newest film Short is behind the usual on day two: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” has 1,387 views at 31.7 an hour, far behind the Ravana Shorts at the same age. Probable cause: the film's audience is thinning (takings fell steeply on its second Monday) and the title is about the film's rule, not a person. Test: day three, 18 November. If it is still under the usual, the film window is closed for Shorts; make no more and give the time to Tipu and Tegh Bahadur.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-14. Long-form is still a Home-feed channel: 145,591 long-form views over 28 days came from the bucket that holds Home and the subscriptions feed, against 3,906 from search. Shorts drew 26.9% of their views from search; the finding that search carries the Shorts has fallen out of range, because the film Shorts rode the Shorts feed.
- The film window is closing in cinemas but not yet in reading. Box-office headlines today report a steep fall on the film's second Monday, while the Ramayana page on English Wikipedia is still at 2.85x its 30-day median. The month's Shorts search terms are still Ravana and Sai Pallavi variants with no long-form behind them.
- The English Wikipedia page on the Great Famine of 1876–1878 is at 7.2x its median, and the data does not show why. The channel already has the Short, “Why Sir Richard Temple Slashed Rations During the 1877 Madras Famine”, at 1,355 views. Nothing new to make this week; the long-form idea below is for after the decisions.
- WhatsApp referred 12,416 views over the 365-day window against Instagram's 442; the base is views from outside YouTube, a small part of all views. When the Indonesia long-form goes public, WhatsApp is where to send it on day one.

## How they are reacting
Under the Ravana Shorts the argument is still about motive, and some viewers now read the film's Ravana as a political hero, which is exactly what the Ravana long-form answers. Under the Asia long-form two arguments are forming, from viewers outside India who claim the epic as theirs and from viewers who read its spread as a loss to Islam. The Indonesia long-form will meet both.
- **The film swapped lust for revenge** (mixed): "the core reason for why he abducted Sita Ji is for lust and arrogance, now in Namit Malhotra's Ramayana they properly showed the arrogance part but replaced lust with revenge which leads to the controversy"
- **Viewers see a political Ravana in the film** (negative): "New movie is woke Ramayana, comrade Ravana freeing oppressed Rakshahas from Deva, they projected Lanka as communist utopia."
- **Viewers already blame E. V. Ramasamy** (negative): "He was the guy that sowed the seeds of political poison in TN, the effects of which impact the people even today."
- **Viewers outside India claim the Ramayana** (positive): "even I'm not indian and Hindu , I'm a Burmese and Buddhist from my home country Myanmar but still big fan of Ramayana"
- **The Asia story read as a loss to Islam** (negative): "Islam destroyed everything 😢"

Requested topics
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Rajendra Chola's fleet to Srivijaya, as the answer to “never sent a single soldier”
- Bagan in Myanmar and its Hindu traces
- The Panchatantra's journey into West Asia

## Competitors
Twelve days after release the watchlist is still on the film, and one outlier now speaks straight to the Ravana question: Upword's Short on a child who liked Ravan more than Shri Ram. Reactions and verdicts on the film are taken. Nobody on the list has traced, with names and dates, where the sympathetic Ravana came from.
- **Upword**: "An eight-year-old watched Ramayana and liked Ravan more than Shri Ram!"
  Why it worked: 23,271 views at 3.9x the channel's median, on the exact feeling the Ravana long-form answers: a viewer who came out of the film on Ravana's side.
  Steal: Put that viewer in the Ravana long-form's title or thumbnail: the person who liked Ravana, and the 1882 book behind the feeling.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 159,991 views at 31.6x, the list's top outlier. It opens by saying the claim it attacks in full, “Diwali is not a Hindu festival. It's a South Asian festival. What?”, and answers from there.
  Steal: Open the Ravana long-form on the sympathetic claim in its own words, said straight, and turn on it in the next sentence.
- **Project SHIVOHAM**: "She's NOT Subhadra? The Forgotten Ancient Goddess"
  Why it worked: A long-form at 260,771 views, 12x its median. It opens on a picture millions hold, the three deities at Puri, and overturns it by the third sentence.
  Steal: A held picture, a question, the reversal at once. For the Ravana long-form the held picture is Ravana as the film shows him.

Gaps
- Where the sympathetic Ravana came from, with names and dates: three own Shorts, an Upword outlier and the month's search terms point at it, and nobody on the list has the long-form.
- Direct Action Day in long-form: the channel's own search data shows demand for “direct action day” arriving only at its three Shorts on it.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, long, 4/5**: Ramayana film, twelve days in: takings falling, reading still up  
  Signal: Box-office headlines today report a steep fall on the second Monday; the Ramayana page on English Wikipedia is still at 2.85x its median. The radar's step for this week is the fact-check long-form. (Moments radar, news, Wikipedia pageviews)  
  Make: This is decision 1, and the window will not wait past this week. Do not let the Indonesia launch push the Ravana long-form past 19 November. The hour it publishes, pin it under the three Ravana Shorts. Judge it on day three.
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: three days, no Short scripted  
  Signal: The Karnataka row over his legacy has been in the news since 11 November (correction: yesterday's brief said 10 November). The radar's step for this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”. (Moments radar, controversy news, owner's note of 15 November)  
  Make: Decision 2, in dates: script today, record 18 November, publish Friday 20 November an hour or two before 18:00 IST, judge on 23 November. Keep “Tipu Sultan” at the front of the title.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November: the radar's step is due now  
  Signal: The top-ranked dated moment, seven days out; the radar's step is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. The radar also lists Tarabai imprisoning Rajaram II on the same date. (Moments radar, calendar)  
  Make: Decision 3, in dates: script by 19 November, record by 21, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26. The working title now carries his name. Skip the Tarabai date: it makes the heroine of one of the channel's biggest Shorts the villain, its date comes from a low-confidence list, and one Short per date is enough.
- **watch, short, 3/5**: Churchill's birth anniversary, 30 November  
  Signal: On the radar thirteen days out. This week's step is research with named sources; the next, on 23 November, is a script. The channel's earlier Churchill Short failed on its opening. (Moments radar, script verdicts)  
  Make: Not a decision yet. Collect named sources for one Churchill order this week; on 23 November, with the Tipu and Tegh Bahadur Shorts out, decide whether it becomes a Short. No long-form on this date: the Ravana long-form holds the slot.
- **watch, short, 2/5**: Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, in cinemas 4 December  
  Signal: A Salman Khan war film whose trailer leads the YouTube chart rows the tracker flagged this week. The radar has no confirmed subject for it. (Moments radar, YouTube chart)  
  Make: Check what real event, if any, the film is about before 20 November, when its first step opens. If it is a real war with an Indian side and a named enemy, it is the next mass-release peg; if it is fiction, skip it.
- **watch, skip, 2/5**: Owner pick: “Ramayana is itihasa, not mythology”  
  Signal: Chosen by the owner on 15 November. Itiha's “Itihasa vs Myth” Short of 3 November stands at 77 views. (Owner's note of 15 November, own Analytics)  
  Make: Not a YouTube Short again; the owner's note sends it to Instagram. See the Instagram section.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [4/5, long] **Who Made Ravana the Wronged Hero? It Began With a British Book in 1882**  
  Decolonization reframe; Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named author convicted from his own page; Contested history  
  source: Decision 1
- [3/5, short] **Tipu Sultan's Death: Who Got Rich From It**  
  Empire and extraction: the prize money and the palace treasure; Contested history: the Karnataka row; Villain plus hypocrisy: the men who took the treasure wrote the verdict on him  
  source: Decision 2. Owner pick of 15 November. Second title on file: “Tipu Sultan Died at This Gate. The British Wrote Everything After”
- [3/5, short] **Guru Tegh Bahadur: Aurangzeb's Order, Chandni Chowk, 1675**  
  Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named emperor and a dated order; Contested history  
  source: Decision 3
- [3/5, long] **Direct Action Day, Calcutta, 16 August 1946: Who Gave the Order**  
  Identity and religion stakes; Villain: a named chief minister, as in the channel's own Suhrawardy Short; Hidden history  
  source: Search gaps: three own Shorts on it draw search every month and no long-form answers it. For after the three decisions.
- [3/5, long] **The Temple Wage: Why Britain Cut Famine Rations in 1877**  
  Empire and extraction; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named governor and his own ration order; Decolonization reframe  
  source: Wikipedia spike on the Great Famine of 1876–1878 and the Short already made on it. For after the three decisions.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,331 followers, up 205 in 7 days, 29.3 a day. The latest reel, “Every Ramayan kept one rule. The New Namit Malhotra film broke it.”, has reached 9,604 with a skip rate of 37.5% against a reel median of 54.1%: it opens on the quarrel, and fewer people swipe past. Carousels remain the growth format at 3.77x the median reach of reels. Owner pick of 15 November, for Instagram only: post “Itihasa vs Myth” as a reel, or a recut that opens on who first filed the Ramayana as mythology.

Do more
- Write carousels in the revision lane  
  52 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 22 for the other lanes (39 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 12.5k, conversion 3.85 vs 2.12 per 1k. 379 followers a month at stake.
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 38 followers (91 posts); outside the band, 12 (13 posts). Pooled rate 3.01 vs 1.4 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 355 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  17 of 102 rated posts are shared above the median (26.9/1k) but convert below it (2.2/1k): median 13.4k reach for a median 13 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 283 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 845 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  86 single images all time: 79.5k reach between them and 113 followers, 1.3 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 160.1. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 93 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: When “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN” goes public, pin one comment under “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?” that answers the Chola correction in a line and points to the new video, and send the new video out on WhatsApp the same day.  
  The Asia long-form is the channel's largest long-form audience, at 348.7 views an hour averaged since release, and the Chola point is its most-liked correction. WhatsApp is the largest outside source of views.
- **this_week**: Look up the Indonesia long-form's scheduled time in Studio and keep at least a day between it and the Ravana long-form.  
  Each long-form is judged on day three; two going up together blur both readings.
- **this_week**: Check “Itihasa vs Myth” and “Is Caste Unique to India?” in Studio for visibility history and restrictions.  
  They stand at 77 and 255 views two weeks on, with days of zero after publish. Still open.
- **later**: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.  
  Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing, so the website is left out today.
